summary:
Design 3 (ZDR) is buildable without breaking any org that does not use ZDR, but ZDR is not usable today for any org. Live facts: 3 orgs, all on plan pro, none has ZDR on; no inference provider is ZDR-attested (all attestation vars empty), so every ZDR chat would be refused; no ZDR request has ever reached the running gateway. An admin can nevertheless switch ZDR on (only the plan is checked) and break chat org-wide.

Recommended architecture. Control Plane (Auth Core) stays the only authority for retention posture. A new per-connection record (capability supported / not_supported / cannot_verify, basis, checked_at, digest) and an append-only acknowledgement ledger live in integration-corev2 next to the connection, written in the same audit transaction as the connection. At turn start the BFF (service-attested) asks Auth Core for a short signed retention decision. Auth Core re-verifies org ZDR, connection ownership and status, capability digest and the stored acknowledgement, then mints the turn's plane tokens with zdr=false plus a connection-bound zdr_waiver claim. Model-gateway and inference-core honour that claim only when the request routes to exactly that connection; any other route is refused, never silently downgraded. Session-core records an immutable receipt on the run row (retention_class=zdr_waived, ack id, connection id). The client can never send zdr=false: only a signed claim can lower the posture. Org ZDR stays on for everyone else, for other connections and for explicit Temporary chat. The org-wide ZDR flag is never written.

Findings that change scope. (1) A token-ZDR turn that selects the subscription route with body zdr=false is silently re-routed by the gateway instead of refused. (2) Auth Core resolves org ZDR to false on any org-core error and caches that for 45 s (token lifetimes 300-900 s). (3) Three readers compute org ZDR differently. (4) ZDR turns are unmetered and show no processing line. (5) The browser retention purge cannot fire. (6) Org ZDR covers interactive content only; connector ingestion, contextual retrieval, graph extraction and memory processing run under persistent service principals on Azure.

ZDR children as metadata-only runs: not the right design. Session-core forces parent_run_id empty on a ZDR start, requires a fresh thread, and refuses ZDR credentials orchestration writes. The HTTP chat path creates no parent run at all. Do and agentic stay refused under ZDR with a typed bilingual reason in v1. A waived run is a normal run, so Do on Terra and its children register normally, which closes the 2026-10-02 finding for the subscription route by construction.

Own API keys do not exist today. The capability record is generic so they plug in later. cannot_verify is a real state; supported is reachable only for Verevon-attested deployments, or later for an explicit org-admin assertion.

Owner decisions that matter most: the waived-run policy for derived jobs (memory index, dreaming, learning review run on Verevon paid providers; recommended skip), the processor-instruction risk of a member overriding an admin's ZDR (no admin lock now, counsel review, optional future control), and gating the ZDR switch on attestation.

# Design 3: ZDR that is workable per org, with per-connection informed consent

Source key: [FACT] read in source or live, [INFERENCE] reasoned from source, [DECISION] owner to decide. Evidence for every fact is in current_state.

## 0. Binding principles (owner rulings)
1. ZDR is on only for orgs that switched it on; we respect it. Orgs without ZDR see no behaviour change at all.
2. A member may use their OWN subscription or API key even if it cannot do ZDR. We check capability when they add it, tell them plainly (stronger warning when their org has ZDR on), let them continue, and turn ZDR off ONLY for runs that use that connection. Never org-wide, never for other members, never for other connections or models.

## 1. Vocabulary and the single rule
O = org ZDR effective (org-core intent AND plan entitlement). R = explicit ZDR on this turn (Temporary chat, x-zdr, body zdr:true). C = the user-owned connection the turn names. K = connection capability: supported | not_supported | cannot_verify, with digest D. A = acknowledgement stored for (org, user, connection, D, text version), not revoked. S = Space ZDR policy (user-core), not applied in chat today.
Run retention class (server-stamped): zdr | persistent | zdr_waived.
Rule: effective_zdr = O AND NOT( run uses C AND K != supported AND A valid AND NOT R AND NOT S ).
- O false: nothing changes, no decision call, no waiver.
- O and no connection named: zdr (org default).
- O and C with K = supported: stays zdr on that connection (future: attested or admin-asserted API keys).
- O and C with K != supported and A valid: run is persistent with a waiver (class zdr_waived), bound to C.
- O and C with K != supported and no valid A: REFUSED with typed code zdr_connection_not_acknowledged. Never silently served, never silently re-routed.
- R (Temporary chat) with C and K != supported: REFUSED (zdr_explicit_request_not_supported_by_connection). A waiver covers the org default only, never an explicit per-turn request. Space ZDR is never waivable.
- Any doubt (Auth Core, org-core or integration-corev2 unreachable): ZDR stays on and the turn is refused with zdr_decision_unavailable (retryable).

### 2.4 Delegation children and the live panel: verdict
Registering ZDR children as metadata-only runs is NOT the right design [INFERENCE from verified rules]: (1) session-core forces parent_run_id empty and requires a fresh thread for any ZDR start, so a ZDR child cannot link to a parent; (2) a ZDR credential cannot write orchestration events (attach_subagent) so no lineage or stop event can exist; (3) the HTTP product path creates no parent run, so there is nothing to attach to; (4) the loop is unreachable under ZDR anyway (gateway and execution-core refuse agentic). ## 3. (B) Connection capability model
Owner of connections and the record: integration-corev2 (Ingestion Plane). Per connection (columns on integration_connections): zdr_capability (supported | not_supported | cannot_verify), zdr_basis, zdr_basis_ref, zdr_checked_at, zdr_digest.
- zdr_basis: verevon_attested_deployment | provider_terms_known | provider_by_contract | customer_asserted (future, admin only) | not_assessed.
- zdr_basis_ref: id of a versioned row in the shared contract api/connection-zdr-capabilities.json, which carries catalog_version. A shared file plus a cross-plane test (integration-corev2 table equals inference-core provider capabilities, for example codex_subscription.rs supports_zdr=false) keeps one source of truth.
- zdr_digest = sha256 of canonical JSON {provider_key, auth_mode, capability, basis, catalog_version}. Any change invalidates acknowledgements automatically.
Today: openai-codex-subscription = not_supported, basis provider_terms_known (Global residency, no ZDR commitment, consumer account terms). Own API key (future): OpenAI, Anthropic and Azure OpenAI keys = cannot_verify, basis provider_by_contract (ZDR exists only by agreement or approval that Verevon cannot see from a key; wording to be confirmed against current vendor docs before copy ships, OD-Z12); unknown or OpenAI-compatible endpoints = cannot_verify; known consumer-plan sign-ins = not_supported. supported is reachable only for Verevon-attested deployments (not connections) and later for an explicit admin assertion with recorded evidence reference (OD-Z5).
Honesty: cannot_verify is a first-class state with its own wording ('we cannot see your agreement with the provider'); it is treated like not_supported by the run rule. Capability is assessed at add (connect start and again at connected) and re-assessed on catalog_version change, on provider reconnect and nightly; a change that alters the digest revokes dependent acknowledgements (reason capability_changed) and audits it.
Existing 5 live connections are backfilled by an idempotent startup job (all in non-ZDR orgs, so no behaviour change).

## 5. (D) Authority and the run-time rule
### 5.1 Authority
Auth Core (Control Plane) decides and mints. Sources it verifies itself: org-core posture (new retention-posture endpoint), and the connection posture from integration-corev2 read AS THE SESSION USER (Auth Core mints a user-bound aud=ingestion token internally from the session; integration-corev2 already enforces owner and org via assertConnectionAccess). No new principal credential, no shared secret, and the BFF cannot assert facts.
Flow per chat turn (only when the body names subscription_connection_id AND the BFF sees org ZDR on):
1. BFF calls POST /api/retention/zdr-decision with an aud=control-policy service token (verevon-gateway gains audience control-policy, scope retention:zdr-decide, retention zdr; pinned by plane-service-principals-policy.contract.spec.ts) plus the user's session cookie and {connection_id, provider, explicit_zdr}. Users cannot call it: no service token.
2. Auth Core resolves O, checks the rule in section 1 and returns {org_zdr, effective_zdr, reason, ack?, decision} where decision is a 60 s RS256 JWT {org, user, connection, ack_id, digest, jti, exp, aud}. Auth Core audits every decision (content-free) with durable PubAck, same pattern as plane_service_token_issued, and refuses to issue if the audit cannot be published.
3. BFF mints its token set with header x-retention-decision on each GET /api/:audience/token (and /api/model-plane/token). Auth Core verifies signature, exp, user equals session user, org equals session org, then stamps claims zdr=false, org_zdr=true, zdr_waiver={connection_id, ack_id, provider, digest, decision_jti} and caps TTL at 300 s. Without the header the tokens carry the org posture (zdr=true): a user minting tokens directly can never obtain a waiver.
4. internal-token and token-exchange routes keep rejecting any x-zdr or body zdr and ignore the decision header; the interactive path ignores x-zdr and body zdr (tested).
The BFF replaces apply_org_zdr_posture with resolve_turn_retention: it never writes zdr=false itself; a client zdr:false or x-zdr:false is ignored (monotonic raise preserved). It maps refusals to typed 409 or 503 JSON.
### 5.2 Per-plane enforcement (what each existing refusal does with a waiver)
- Shared pure resolver in mp-contracts (new retention.rs): inputs claims view (zdr, org_zdr, waiver) plus request route (provider, connection, explicit zdr) gives Zdr | Persistent | Waived{connection, ack} | Refuse(code). Gateway, inference-core, execution-core and session-core call it; Go and TypeScript planes run the same golden matrix.
- model-gateway: claims gain org_zdr and zdr_waiver; claims.zdr stays required. normalize uses claims-aware ZDR: with a waiver the request must be provider openai-codex-subscription with exactly the bound connection and no explicit zdr, else 403 zdr_waiver_route_mismatch; without a waiver and token ZDR a subscription request is refused typed. All ~20 effective_zdr sites call the resolver (source-scan test). Delegated bearers must carry equal zdr and equal waiver or the request is refused (posture mismatch). Usage frame is stamped retention_class from the VERIFIED claim.
- inference-core: backstop. A principal with a waiver may only invoke provider_hint openai-codex-subscription with the bound connection id; everything else (other providers, embeddings, speech, vision) gets PermissionDenied zdr_waiver_route_mismatch. Missing zdr claim is rejected.
- session-core: VerifiedIdentity.zdr_waiver. start_managed_run records an immutable receipt on the run: retention_class zdr_waived, waiver_ack_id, waiver_connection_id (new migration 0043); caller.zdr false, so thread, messages, completion and memory are durable. This is a receipt of what applied at start, not the live org posture, which stays owned by Control Plane (proof-bundle 'retained' section is updated to cite the receipt). Child runs started by execution-core under the run's own bearer inherit the claim.
- execution-core: enforce_persistence_free_execution and validate_run_route pass because zdr is false; add waiver binding (provider_hint and connection must equal the claim). Children use the same ModelRoute, so they cannot leave the connection.
- Data Plane, capability-core, letta-bridge, sandbox, cost: tokens have zdr=false, behave as non-ZDR. Retrieval therefore runs in persistent mode for the waived run (dense arm works), which the acknowledgement text states.
- Quarry: body zdr is set by gateway and execution-core from the RUN's resolved posture (false for a waived run); Z-08 also ORs the token claim in as a floor.
### 5.3 What the waiver can never do
Never org-wide (no org-core write), never for other members (decision requires session user equals ack user equals connection owner), never for other connections or routes (route binding at gateway, inference-core, execution-core), never for explicit Temporary chat, Space ZDR, scheduled or unattended runs, inbox or support AI, browser runs, speech, or non-chat endpoints.

## 7. (F) Security analysis
- Spoofing: only Auth Core signs the waiver; the BFF cannot assert it; client zdr:false is ignored; waiver tokens are bound to one connection and checked at gateway, inference-core and execution-core, so a leaked waiver token cannot reach another provider.
- Replay: decision 60 s with jti, tokens 300 s max, both bound to the cookie session user and org; replay without the session adds nothing. Mint also needs the BFF service token.
- Member impersonation: acknowledgement requires owner equals actor; decision requires session user equals ack user equals connection.user_id and connection org equals session org; the broker re-checks org and user at call time.
- Revocation: owner can revoke any time; effect on the next decision; an in-flight turn finishes (token at most 300 s); runs already persisted stay persisted (stated in the text). Connection removal revokes (reason connection_removed). Capability or text change invalidates via digest.
- Stale acknowledgement: digest and min text version compared at decision time, not at ack time.
- Confused deputy: Quarry, Data Plane and tools take posture from the run's verified claim; waiver tokens do not exist outside the BFF chat handlers; gateway helper calls already inherit the route; any call outside the route is refused, not rerouted.
- Org-core or Auth Core outage: ZDR kept, turn refused (zdr_decision_unavailable). Auth Core stale-if-error posture removes the current fail-open.
- Processor-instruction risk [FACT-based, legal]: a member can override an admin's ZDR for their own runs, which sends org data to the provider under the member's own terms. Mitigations: explicit text, audit, admin visibility, no waiver for unattended work. Counsel review and an optional admin control are tracked (OD-Z4).
- Ack record is personal data: kept while the connection exists and 365 days after revoke (audit retention), erased with the org purge.

## 8. What a waived run persists (explicit) and what is keyed to the run
A waived run is a normal persistent run: thread, messages, run, plan, events, approvals, child runs and lineage, response cache, feedback, usage envelope (cost basis subscription). Exclusions are keyed to the RUN or token, never the org: learning events use the run's outbox zdr; dreaming reads persisted messages; memory uses MemoryRetention::of(caller token); caches use the request flag; Quarry uses the body flag the gateway sets from the run. Derived processing that calls Verevon-operated providers is a separate widening: memory indexing (agent memory server on Azure), dreaming, learning review (claude-sonnet-4-5) and Data Plane query embedding would send the waived run's content to providers the user did not accept. Recommended default [DECISION OD-Z2]: persist the conversation, but skip memory indexing, dreaming and learning review for retention_class zdr_waived (matches the open OD4 recommendation for subscription threads); the acknowledgement text lists what stays on (saved chat, knowledge search, Do tools).

rollout_and_migration:
Principle: zero impact on any org that does not use ZDR. Today none of the 3 live orgs has ZDR on and no ZDR request has ever been served, so every step below can ship dark.

Order (planes first, authority last, UI last):
1. Wave 0 stop-gaps (Z-00 to Z-09) ship independently. They only add refusals or fixes for ZDR paths, and move Auth Core to stale-if-error. Z-04 prevents enabling a ZDR mode that nothing can serve.
2. Shared fixtures and resolver (Z-10, Z-11), then every plane learns the waiver claim and enforces route binding while it is never minted: inference-core and model-gateway (Z-15, Z-16), session-core receipt (Z-17), execution-core (Z-18). A plane that predates the claim ignores it and would treat a waiver token as an ordinary non-ZDR token, so Auth Core must not mint until all four report the waiver contract version (launcher check, Z-32).
3. integration-corev2 schema, assessor, backfill and acknowledgement API (Z-12, Z-13). Migration 0013 is additive. Backfill marks the 5 live connections not_supported and writes no acknowledgements. A revert drops only the new table and columns.
4. Auth Core decision endpoint behind ZDR_WAIVER_ENABLED=false (Z-14). With the flag off the endpoint answers waiver_disabled; acknowledgements can be recorded (consent only) but no waiver is minted, so a ZDR org member gets the typed refusal. Kill switch: flip the flag, tokens revert to org posture on the next mint (at most 300 s for tokens already issued).
5. BFF (Z-19) and Frontend (Z-20): until the flag is on the UI shows the prompt but chats stay refused with a clear reason. Z-32 wires env, the control-policy scope for verevon-gateway (pinned by the real-file contract spec) and the launcher gate.
6. Turn the flag on only for the proof window on the dedicated test org (Z-60), then leave on once the evidence note passes.

Control Plane dependencies (explicit): org-core retention-posture endpoint (Z-03), Auth Core stale-if-error (Z-02), the decision endpoint, claim and registry row (Z-14), launcher and compose changes (Z-32), and a new read edge Auth Core to integration-corev2 recorded in the contract matrix. Builds go through the launcher only (hand-built compose misses the Control Plane env chain).

Data migration: existing connections get capability columns by backfill; existing tokens, runs and threads are untouched; session-core gets nullable retention receipt columns with default persistent, so old rows read as persistent. No ZDR org exists to migrate. If an org enables ZDR later, existing durable data stays (forward-looking, now stated in the tooltip).

Backward compatibility: waiver claims are additive JWT fields. The only behaviour change for non-ZDR orgs is stricter claim validation (Z-01) and clearer refusals; Z-01 must be preceded by a check that every live token carries zdr (Auth Core always sets it).

Not shipped until the owner acts: provider attestation (Z-40) and own-API-key connections (Z-50); ZDR chat itself stays unusable without Z-40, which is why Z-04 gates the switch.
risks: INCIDENT: during read-only verification one command printed the first 40 characters of CODEX_SUBSCRIPTION_INTERNAL_API_KEY (inference-core container env) into this session's tool output. The value is not repeated anywhere in this result, but the key is effectively disclosed to this transcript. Rotate it (integration-api and Model Plane share it) before relying on it.

Processor-instruction risk: a member can override an org admin's ZDR choice for their own runs, sending org data to a provider under the member's own terms. GDPR_SUMMARY denies model providers for ZDR content unless they satisfy ZDR, so this is a documented policy exception that needs counsel review; no admin lock is designed (owner not ruled).

Processor widening inside a waived run: Verevon-operated Azure and Anthropic calls on the run's content (query embedding for grounding, memory indexing on azure/gpt-4o-mini, learning review on claude-sonnet-4-5, dreaming) are outside the waiver the user accepts. Mitigated only if OD-Z2 (skip derived jobs) is adopted; grounding embedding still runs in persistent mode and is named in the acknowledgement text.

Rollout skew: an old plane that ignores the waiver claim treats a waiver token as ordinary non-ZDR with no route binding. Mitigated by flag-off default, planes-first order and a launcher gate; inference-core is the backstop for every route.

Waiver-bearing session-core and data-plane tokens are valid for up to 300 s and cannot be route-bound by those planes. Exposure is limited to the BFF (decision needs the BFF service token plus the session cookie) and TTL; a BFF compromise or SSRF would widen it.

Provider ZDR facts for API-key vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI) are my knowledge of vendor practice, not repo evidence, and may be stale after June 2026; wording must be confirmed against current vendor documents and counsel before shipping (OD-Z12).

The subscription-route claim 'no ZDR' rests on repo declarations (codex_subscription.rs) and consumer-plan terms, not on a vendor statement; if OpenAI changes ChatGPT-plan terms the shared capability file and catalog_version must change, and every acknowledgement then goes stale by digest (intended).

Auth Core now depends on integration-corev2 and org-core at decision time; an outage refuses waived turns (typed, retryable) rather than guessing. Latency is paid only by ZDR-org members who name a subscription connection.

Auth Core stale-if-error (Z-02) changes the outage behaviour for non-ZDR orgs only when a ZDR org was last known; an Auth Core cold start during an org-core outage still mints persistent (availability-first) and must alert (OD-Z10).

ZDR chat remains unusable until a provider is attested (Z-40) and, for grounding, an embedding path is ZDR-capable or degraded explicitly (Z-41); the L12 mismatch (index built with Cohere, queries must match) limits options.

Metering ZDR turns (Z-06) adds an org-level metadata-only envelope under ZDR; it must carry no user id, no prompt, no request text, and needs the owner's approval (OD-Z7) before any envelope allowlist is added.

Sources not proven live: every ZDR path (stream, unary, gRPC, Data Plane ephemeral retrieval, learning skip) was verified by source and tests only because no ZDR token or org exists; findings 2 and the retrieval degrade behaviour are source-verified, not live.

Space ZDR (user-core effective policy, 0 rows live) is not applied to chat provider choice today (L14); when it is, a waiver must not override it. The golden matrix carries Space rows now so the day it is enforced the test fails first.
Acknowledgement records are personal data; retention and erasure must be defined (kept while the connection exists plus 365 days after revoke, purged with the org) and added to the org purge path.
Dual registries (bootstrap script versus Control Plane file) can drift and silently change per-audience retention; reconcile in Z-32.
A member who revokes mid-run: the turn completes and the persisted run stays persisted; the acknowledgement text says so, and users may expect deletion. Product wording must be exact.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z1: Scope of the waiver. May it cover only the org-level ZDR default, never an explicit Temporary chat, never a Space ZDR policy, and only interactive owner-present chat turns (not scheduled, support, inbox, browser, speech)?
owner_decisions.options: A) Org default only, interactive chat only (as designed). B) Also allow Temporary chat to be waived. C) Also allow unattended runs on the owner's connection.
owner_decisions.recommended: A. A waiver is a downgrade of the org default for one owner-present turn; explicit per-turn ZDR and Space policy are stronger statements and stay respected.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z2: What may a waived (persisted) run feed into? Memory indexing, dreaming and learning review call Verevon-operated paid providers (Azure, claude-sonnet-4-5) the user never accepted.
owner_decisions.options: A) Normal non-ZDR behaviour (everything on, subject to existing switches). B) Persist the conversation but skip memory indexing, dreaming and learning review for retention_class zdr_waived. C) Do not persist at all (not what the owner asked).
owner_decisions.recommended: B. It matches the open OD4 recommendation for subscription-route threads and keeps the waiver from widening to providers the user did not choose; the acknowledgement text lists exactly what stays on.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z3: Acknowledgement lifecycle.
owner_decisions.options: A) No time expiry; invalid on capability digest change, text-version bump, connection removal or owner revoke. B) Re-confirm every 90 or 180 days. C) Re-confirm per session.
owner_decisions.recommended: A for v1, with a min text version setting so a material wording change forces re-confirmation.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z4: Admin control and legal exposure. A member can override the admin's ZDR for their own runs; as processor, instructions come from the org. Add an org setting 'members may use own connections without ZDR' (default on) now or later?
owner_decisions.options: A) None now; audit plus admin visibility only. B) Ship the org switch now (default on). C) Default off (admin must allow).
owner_decisions.recommended: A now, B on the roadmap before the first regulated customer org, and counsel review of the exception (GDPR_SUMMARY amendment). No lock is built without your ruling.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z5: cannot_verify handling and customer assertion for own API keys (future).
owner_decisions.options: A) cannot_verify is treated as non-ZDR (waiver needed); no customer assertion. B) Same, plus an org-admin-only 'asserted by admin, not verified' state that keeps ZDR on for that connection. C) Trust any user claim.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z6: Gate enabling org ZDR on an attested provider (server-enforced 409 zdr_no_attested_provider).
owner_decisions.options: A) Gate (as designed). B) Allow enabling and let chat fail. C) Allow with a warning only.
owner_decisions.recommended: A. All 3 live orgs are entitled and nothing is attested, so B or C is a one-click org-wide outage.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z7: Metering ZDR turns.
owner_decisions.options: A) Org-level metadata-only usage envelope (tokens, latency, model, no user id, no request text) plus an org-level budget check. B) Per-user metadata. C) No metering.
owner_decisions.recommended: A, because ZDR is a paid add-on and the matrix already assigns 'ZDR/cost metadata only'; C leaves paid inference unbilled and unbudgeted.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z8: Do mode and delegation children under real ZDR.
owner_decisions.options: A) Refuse with a typed bilingual reason in v1; register no children (as designed); waived runs get normal children. B) Build ephemeral orchestration (contentless subagent frames, no session-core write). C) Register ZDR children as metadata-only runs.
owner_decisions.recommended: A now, B only if customers need Do under ZDR. C is not valid in the current session-core model: ZDR start forces parent_run_id empty and a fresh thread and ZDR credentials cannot write orchestration events.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z9: Scope of org ZDR relative to ingestion.
owner_decisions.options: A) Interactive content only, stated plainly in the tooltip, /trust and the pack; no change to connector sync. B) Also treat synced documents as restricted when the org has ZDR (kills contextualization, graph and dense retrieval for that org).
owner_decisions.recommended: A now, revisit B when an attested embedding resource exists (Z-41).

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z10: Auth Core behaviour when org-core is unreachable and no last-known posture exists.
owner_decisions.options: A) Mint persistent (availability-first) with an alert, plus 24 h stale-if-error from last known. B) Mint ZDR (privacy-first), which turns every org's chat persistence off during an org-core outage.
owner_decisions.recommended: A with stale-if-error; escalate to B only for orgs previously known to be ZDR (which stale-if-error already covers).

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z11: Home of the acknowledgement ledger and the new Auth Core read edge.
owner_decisions.options: A) integration-corev2 next to the connection (atomic invalidation and audit; Auth Core reads it as the session user). B) org-core ledger with NATS-driven invalidation. C) session-core.
owner_decisions.recommended: A: acknowledgement is a per-connection consent (precedent integration_connection_consents), and capability change, disconnect and audit then share one transaction. Record the new Control to Ingestion read edge in the contract matrix.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z12: Who signs the per-provider ZDR wording and the legal text of the acknowledgement (NO and EN), including vendor claims for OpenAI, Anthropic and Azure API accounts?
owner_decisions.options: A) Counsel plus engineering confirm against current vendor documents before copy ships. B) Ship engineering wording and review later.
owner_decisions.recommended: A, for the ChatGPT subscription text as well; drafts in the design are placeholders.

owner_decisions.question: OD-Z13: Which deployment to attest first (operator and contract action, Z-40).
owner_decisions.options: A) Azure OpenAI Sweden Central chat deployment plus a matching embedding path. B) Chat only; knowledge grounding stays lexical-only under ZDR with a notice. C) Wait.
owner_decisions.recommended: A if the signed no-retention approval covers both; otherwise B, because ZDR chat without any attestation is unusable and Z-04 will keep the switch disabled.
